D021-D016_h001.question: I’m a 45-year-old psychiatric ward nurse, divorced, and lately, things have been… really difficult. I find myself constantly thinking about every single thing I eat. My mind is just consumed with food, particularly how certain foods, like anything with carbs or fats, will instantly make me gain weight. It’s not just a thought; it's a deep-seated fear that I believe with every fiber of my being. I’ve cut my daily intake down to practically nothing, maybe a small salad or a piece of fruit. I know it’s not much, and I’m objectively underweight, but I just can’t bring myself to eat more. I still look in the mirror and see someone who needs to lose more, and the thought of gaining even a pound is terrifying. It’s been going on for over six months now, and honestly, the obsessive thoughts about food are all because of this intense dread of getting fat.
D021-D016_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D021-D016_h002.question:
Lately, I’ve just felt…consumed. It started subtly, maybe six or seven months ago, but now it's all I can think about. I’ve been intentionally skipping meals, mostly lunch, sometimes breakfast, because every bite feels like it's going to make me balloon. My husband, bless his heart, tries to get me to eat, but I just can't. The numbers on the scale have been steadily dropping, and even though I'm getting smaller, I still look in the mirror and just see certain parts that are still too big. It’s like a constant battle in my head.

I weigh myself multiple times a day, every single morning and before bed. If the number even nudges up a tiny bit, I get this intense panic. I’ll start rearranging the jewelry displays at the shop, moving things around just to keep my mind off it, but it always comes back to my weight. It feels like my thoughts about food and my body are always there, and it’s truly because I'm terrified of gaining weight and how my body might look if I do. I know it's affecting my energy; I get lightheaded sometimes when I'm helping customers, but the fear of gaining back even a pound is stronger than anything else.
D021-D016_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D021-D016_h003.question: It’s been pretty rough lately, Doc. I’ve dropped a lot of weight, and it just keeps going down, even though I've already lost so much. It’s like, I can’t stop thinking about food, but it’s not in a good way. Every time I even consider eating something that isn’t ‘safe,’ my mind races with thoughts about how it’ll go straight to my gut and make me huge. I know it sounds crazy, but the thought of gaining even a pound terrifies me. I spend hours planning my meals, calculating every single bite, just to make sure I don't mess up and get fat. It's exhausting, but I have to do it, because I’m so scared of how I’ll look if I don’t.
D021-D016_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D021-D016_h004.question: "Well, doctor, it's gotten pretty bad. I've been skipping meals for months now, sometimes breakfast, sometimes supper. If that number ticks up even a tiny bit, a fraction of a pound, I get this intense panic. It's like a siren going off in my head. All these thoughts about food and what I'm eating, or not eating, they're always there, every single moment, and it's all because I'm absolutely terrified of gaining even an ounce. I can't stand the idea of looking bigger, of not being in control of my size."
D021-D016_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder

D021-D016_h005.question: "Lately, cooking, which used to be my passion, has become a relentless torment. I look in the mirror and still see areas I need to trim down. The thought of eating anything rich, like even a piece of bread, fills me with such dread. That fear of gaining even an ounce, of feeling my body change shape, that's what drives all these thoughts about food and what I can and can't eat. It’s like a constant battle in my head."

A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Bipolar II Disorder
